children: Micron Technology Inc. (MU, Financials), the memory-chip maker, fell alongside other memory stocks after Samsung Electronics reported record earnings that still came in below elevated market expectations.
Premarket trading in the US saw a 2.6% decline in Micron shares, a 2.6% decline in SanDisk shares, and a 1.9% decline in SK Hynix shares.
The average forecast was 86.13 trillion won for Samsung's net profit, but the company only managed 75.14 trillion won.
Operating profit increased by over nine times to 107.44 trillion won, while revenue increased by more than double to 195.25 trillion won, a new record.
Regardless of those increases, investors in Seoul were more concerned with the earnings loss and the lack of information surrounding shareholder payouts, causing Samsung shares to fall more than 4%.
As a whole, the lesson for memory stocks was contradictory.

According to Samsung, price will be supported by tight supply conditions for several years. Additionally, it anticipates that next year will see continued high demand for high-bandwidth memory, especially HBM4.
Even while the supply backdrop is still positive for Micron and SanDisk, the selloff has shown that solid fundamentals might not be sufficient in the face of already high expectations.
The next event that might cause a price spike is if future memory profits show that demand for AI and prices are still robust enough to sustain the present values.

title: Micron and SanDisk Fall as Samsung Selloff Hits Memory Stocks
